item.title: BACK IN HISTORY | New $30m boiler for sugar mill
item.description: Back in May of 1994, The Fiji Times had reported that the Fiji Sugar Corporation was planning to undertake about $70 million worth of new projects over five years. Corporation chairman Lyle Cupit made the announcement while inspecting a newly commissioned $30 million boiler at the Lautoka mill.
item.content:encoded:
Back in May of 1994, The Fiji Times had reported that the Fiji Sugar Corporation was planning to undertake about $70 million worth of new projects over five years.

Corporation chairman Lyle Cupit made the announcement while inspecting a newly commissioned $30 million boiler at the Lautoka mill.

He said the corporation’s board would soon approve the new five-year plan with hopes of earning sufficient returns from the mills to finance the projects.

“With our present earnings, we might have to borrow money to implement the project, and this is causing concern,” Mr Cupit said.

He said the mill’s new multi-million Thomson boiler, which consisted of a 12-megawatt turbogenerator, a water treatment plant, and an upgraded electricity supply system, would be operational for the 1994 crushing season scheduled to start on June 7 of that year.

He said the boiler was the most modern available and should prove highly efficient and beneficial, and that the Lautoka mill would then operate with three boilers, and the other old, small Thomson boilers would be dismantled.

Mr Cupit said the board recognised steam and power-generating facilities had been a constraint to proper crushing operations at Lautoka, and that approval for the boiler had come in 1992 after a study by the corporation’s head office technical team.

He added that a $600,000 water treatment plant would hopefully curb water supply problems faced by the mill the previous season.

He revealed that since its inception, the corporation had spent over $235m on capital projects, with over $105m spent in the previous five years alone.

Mr Cupit said the corporation had the responsibility to ensure the continued viability of its factories and had continued to improve factory operations, increase crushing rates, shorten crushing seasons, and increase efficiency.

“With current pressure on the sugar industry in the world environment, changes will be necessary, including rationalisation of operations to ensure that the corporation remains competitive.”

Mr Cupit said the corporation looked forward to everyone’s support to make the 1994 crushing season a successful one.

He was accompanied on his tour by Lautoka mill general manager Ram Karan Singh, chief advising engineer John Korma, and factory manager William Thaggard.

item.title: Solar program extends coverage
item.description: A regional initiative to equip Pacific communities with practical renewable energy skills is continuing to expand after completing its third solar photovoltaic (PV) installation in Fiji. The Fiji Solar Scholars program has trained 14 participants from Fiji, Vanuatu and Tuvalu to plan, install and manage basic solar PV systems, with graduates now applying their skills in community projects.
item.content:encoded:
A regional initiative to equip Pacific communities with practical renewable energy skills is continuing to expand after completing its third solar photovoltaic (PV) installation in Fiji.

The Fiji Solar Scholars program has trained 14 participants from Fiji, Vanuatu and Tuvalu to plan, install and manage basic solar PV systems, with graduates now applying their skills in community projects.

The latest installation at the Fiji Council of Social Services (FCOSS) headquarters in Suva follows earlier projects at Yavulo Kindergarten in Sigatoka and the FCOSS Western Office in Lautoka.

The program was delivered in May this year by 350.org Pacific in partnership with the Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities to make renewable energy expertise more accessible to grassroots communities.

350.org Pacific and Caribbean program lead Fenton Lutunatabua said the initiative was designed to help communities respond to growing economic and climate challenges.

“Distributed solar energy has the potential to address the high cost of living, energy poverty, and disaster response needs,” he said.

Mr Lutunatabua said while Pacific leaders continued to advocate internationally for climate finance and a transition away from fossil fuels, communities could also take practical steps through locally managed renewable energy projects.

item.title: Hill likely to give evidence
item.description: FITNESS trainer Jonathan Hill will “most likely” give evidence if the Suva Magistrate’s Court finds he has a case to answer on a charge of unlawful possession of methamphetamine. His lawyer Shirley Tivao informed Magistrate Sufia Hamza of this yesterday after the court fixed a two-day trial date beginning on November 2.
item.content:encoded:
FITNESS trainer Jonathan Hill will “most likely” give evidence if the Suva Magistrate’s Court finds he has a case to answer on a charge of unlawful possession of methamphetamine.

His lawyer Shirley Tivao informed Magistrate Sufia Hamza of this yesterday after the court fixed a two-day trial date beginning on November 2.

Mr Hill and co-accused Pauliasi Tagicakiviti are jointly charged with one count of unlawful possession of 0.5381 grams of methamphetamine. They are also charged with possession of property suspected to be proceeds of crime after Mr Hill was allegedly found with $400 while Mr Tagicakiviti was found with $1620.

Both offences were alleged to have occurred in Lami on March 1, 2023.

Prosecutors informed the court that neither accused made any admission during their caution interviews and that the State intended to call 13 witnesses during trial.

The matter has been adjourned to September 2.

item.title: Defence says no case to answer
item.description: LAWYERS representing six people charged over an alleged drug operation have argued there is no case for their clients to answer, submitting that the prosecution has failed to produce sufficient evidence to establish the essential elements of the charges. The submissions were made before Magistrate Sufia Hamza after the close of the prosecution’s case yesterday.
item.content:encoded:
LAWYERS representing six people charged over an alleged drug operation have argued there is no case for their clients to answer, submitting that the prosecution has failed to produce sufficient evidence to establish the essential elements of the charges.

The submissions were made before Magistrate Sufia Hamza after the close of the prosecution’s case yesterday.

The accused are Ginna Choi, Josua Ravula, Yu Yang Fang, Minghui Dai, Zhou Lan and Peniasi Ganilau Delai.

The lawyers argued there was no evidence linking their clients to the drugs allegedly seized during police raids at Flagstaff and along Rewa St in Suva in September last year.

They further argued that key police witnesses gave inconsistent accounts of the search, the discovery of the drugs and the handling of exhibits, submitting that the discrepancies undermined the reliability of the State’s case.

Mr Ravula is accused of possessing 42.295 grams of methamphetamine, while Ms Choi and Mr Delai are accused of possessing 0.345 grams. Ms Choi is also alleged to have had $977.60, $US4 and 200 Philippine pesos, suspected to be proceeds of crime.

Chinese nationals Yu Yang Fang, Minghui Dai, and Zhou Lan are charged with possessing 39.509 grams of methamphetamine. Mr Zhou is also accused of being in possession of $7180, $US60, $HK1520, and 600 Chinese yuan, suspected to be proceeds of crime.

Mr Yu faces charges of dealing methamphetamine with others and possessing $906.25, also suspected to be proceeds of crime.

State prosecutor Eoghn Samisoni, however, defended the charges, maintaining there was sufficient evidence for all the accused to answer to the charges.

Ms Hamza will deliver her decision on August 13.

item.title: Court hears of ‘gruesome, relentless murder’
item.description: A “gruesome and relentless murder” was how Dr Isireli Biumaitotoya met his death in his home in Nadi last year, the High Court in Lautoka was told yesterday. Delivering his closing submissions yesterday, Deputy Director of Public Prosecutions John Rabuku said the State had proven beyond reasonable doubt that accused Ratu Peceli Rokoralovo intended to kill the medical practitioner.
item.content:encoded:
A “gruesome and relentless murder” was how Dr Isireli Biumaitotoya met his death in his home in Nadi last year, the High Court in Lautoka was told yesterday.

Delivering his closing submissions yesterday, Deputy Director of Public Prosecutions John Rabuku said the State had proven beyond reasonable doubt that accused Ratu Peceli Rokoralovo intended to kill the medical practitioner.

The State called more than 27 witnesses and tendered 15 exhibits to support allegations that Mr Rokoralovo murdered Dr Biumaitotoya between August 31 and September 1, last year.

Mr Rabuku said the evidence showed the accused repeatedly attacked the doctor with a long-handled cane knife at the latter’s Namaka home.

“The evidence of each witness called by the State was never shaken or discredited during cross-examination,” he said.

He argued the pathologist’s findings of about 30 knife wounds, including skull fractures, demonstrated a sustained attack and an intention to kill rather than self-defence or provocation.

“Thirty plus strikes is not proportional. It exceeds necessity.”

The prosecutor also alleged the accused drove the victim’s vehicle to Nausori after the incident, picking up passengers, refuelling and later returning the vehicle to the doctor’s home before leaving.

Mr Rabuku said this conduct was inconsistent with the defence of self-defence and showed the accused acted “without a care in the world” while the doctor lay dead.

He urged Justice Aruna Aluthge to find the accused guilty of murder, saying the State’s evidence was overwhelming.

The defence has been given seven days to file its response to the State’s closing submissions. Judgment is scheduled to be delivered on August 18.

item.title: Court suspends man’s three-year jail term
item.description: THE High Court has suspended the three-year jail sentence of a man who attempted to burn down his family home while his 68-year-old father was inside. Justice Daniel Goundar sentenced Titoko Cabobula Nasema, 29, who pleaded guilty to one count of attempted arson relating to an incident at Nadonumai Settlement, Lami, on March 21 this year.
item.content:encoded:
THE High Court has suspended the three-year jail sentence of a man who attempted to burn down his family home while his 68-year-old father was inside.

Justice Daniel Goundar sentenced Titoko Cabobula Nasema, 29, who pleaded guilty to one count of attempted arson relating to an incident at Nadonumai Settlement, Lami, on March 21 this year.

The court heard that on this day, Nasema threatened to burn the house during an argument while both were drinking alcohol. He then poured premix fuel inside the house, sprinkled some on his father and repeatedly flicked a lighter before setting the fuel alight.

The fire began burning while his father remained inside the house, but it was extinguished before causing significant damage.

The court heard Nasema’s father had forgiven him and confirmed that since being released on bail, his son had supported him and his wife with household tasks and other assistance.

Justice Goundar noted that Nasema was the person who pulled his father out of the burning house.

item.title: Boy was murdered, police confirm
item.description: THE death of a 12-year-old boy whose body was found near his Wailoku home is being treated as murder as investigations continue, police said. The victim, Lote Qima, was reported missing after he failed to return home from a neighbour’s house where he was last seen playing on Wednesday night last week.
item.content:encoded:
THE death of a 12-year-old boy whose body was found near his Wailoku home is being treated as murder as investigations continue, police said.

The victim, Lote Qima, was reported missing after he failed to return home from a neighbour’s house where he was last seen playing on Wednesday night last week.

His mother later lodged a missing person’s report, prompting a search by family members and police.

The search ended when the boy’s body was discovered near the family home at around midday on Saturday.

Police have since taken a 17-year-old boy into custody for questioning in relation to the case.

The juvenile is being interviewed in the presence of a guardian, in accordance with legal requirements.

A 29-year-old man who had earlier been taken in for questioning has since been released.

Police said investigations into the circumstances surrounding the boy’s death were continuing.

The case has shocked the Wailoku community as detectives work to establish the events leading to the alleged murder.

item.title: Man denies allegation
item.description: A man accused of murdering his pregnant de-facto partner last year told the High Court yesterday he did not tell police officers of not regretting his alleged offence. Daniel Francis Prasad, 47, is standing trial at the High Court in Lautoka before Justice Aruna Aluthge on one count of murder.
item.content:encoded:
A man accused of murdering his pregnant de-facto partner last year told the High Court yesterday he did not tell police officers of not regretting his alleged offence.

Daniel Francis Prasad, 47, is standing trial at the High Court in Lautoka before Justice Aruna Aluthge on one count of murder.

Mr Prasad is alleged to have fatally stabbed his 28-year-old partner at their home in Kerebula, Nadi, on April 27, 2025.

During cross-examination yesterday, State prosecutor Joeli Nasa suggested to the accused that he had told officers at the Nadi Police Station that he did not regret what he did.

In response, Mr Prasad denied making those remarks at the police station.

Mr Nasa also told the accused that he had obtained a Domestic Violence Restraining Order (DVRO) in October 2024, due to ongoing disputes and conflicts between himself and his partner.

In response, Mr Prasad claimed his partner had assaulted him which prompted him to file for the order.

The prosecution alleged that Mr Prasad’s son had witnessed his father killing his partner with a cane knife.

Defence lawyer Edwin Wainiqolo asked his client if he loved the victim.

Mr Prasad replied saying he loved his partner as she was a caring person and loved his three children.

The matter has been adjourned to August 19 for closing submissions.
